name: Once, From Behind
description: Tithe-day at Moreva is tomorrow, and the Tallymen's collector sleeps on the south boards beside the strongbox that holds his tithe-book, which says Moreva owes forty baskets it never caught. Sauve Mor, who lifts a hundred and forty eel-traps before dawn and sells to Gullhithe through a man he has never met, means to have the book before the collector wakes. He teaches by being unseen and then being behind you: past the night-watch to his traps, the strongbox and the sleeping man's pocket, a dagger and a sack of eels, and at first grey, in the fog, the collector's bravo.
notes: The rogue's tutorial (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.4, 3.4a), begun by core:opening/rogue, reworked for triage 44 (PROGRESS.md, 'The Rogue's first quest makes sense, and its stealth can be done'). One goal runs through it: take the collector's tithe-book (core:item/tithe_book, in the strongbox's loot core:loot/tithe_strongbox) before he and his bravo wake. The traps: Tella Oul (the Reed Council's night-watch, a lantern on her: the stage's `unseen`, NightWatch) stands at the head of the way down to the South Channel looking down it; the lane on the way's east side is sheltered from her by four `cover` props (QuestCover: stacked crates, eel-traps and an upturned boat); the straight way down passes six metres in front of her lantern. Seen, you go back into the lane's shelter (the nearest `back_to`), not to the start. Sauve walks down openly (she knows him) and is `with_you_when` the quest is active, so the HUD's eye reads the watch and not him. The strongbox is a QuestSpots prop (a locked WorldContainer the Tallymen own) opened on the lockpick screen (`pick_lock`); the collector (core:npc/tithe_collector) sleeps beside it through the three night lessons, and lifting from his pocket is the optional `pickpocket` act. The sack is a Pell of kind sack, which never sees anybody, so a crouched blow from behind is a sneak attack. The bravo walks the landing's round at first grey (QuestFoes, `round`), in fog. test_rogue_plays plays it with the body and the keys.

stages.journal:
Tomorrow is tithe-day at Moreva. The Tallymen's collector, Brannock Tole, came in last night with his strongbox, his tithe-book and his bravo, and he sleeps on the south boards beside the box. His book says Moreva owes forty baskets more than it caught, and the Charter believes the book, not the eels. Sauve Mor means to have that book before the collector wakes, and first he wants to see whether you can move on the boards without being seen.

Tella Oul keeps the Reed Council's night-watch at the head of the way down to the South Channel, with a lantern, looking down the way to the water. She knows Sauve. She does not know you, and a stranger on the boards on tithe-eve is somebody she has to report at the count. Crouch, keep the stacked traps and the old boat on the east side of the way between you and her lantern, and meet Sauve at his traps on the channel's edge.

Crouched, the corner of your eye says what she has of you: Unseen, Noticed, Seen. Noticed, stop, get something between you and her, and let her forget you. Seen, go back into the shelter of the stacks and come again.

said: You! On the boards! Who's that, low there?
Seen. Back behind the stacks, and keep still till she's looking at the water again.
again: She's looking at the water. Again: lower, and the stacks between you.

say: Low. Now down the east side, behind the traps and the boat. She knows me. She doesn't know you.

objectives.text: Get down to Sauve at the South Channel's traps without Tella seeing you

stages.journal:
Sauve has lifted his traps. Now the book. It is in the collector's strongbox on the landing's south-east boards, and Brannock Tole is asleep against it with one hand on his waistcoat pocket. Go back up crouched, pick the strongbox's lock (the pin sets as the needle crosses the band), and take the tithe-book out of it.

A lock picked is a crime, and a crime seen is a bounty. Tella is still at the head of the way with her lantern, so do it where she cannot see. And if you have the hands for it, his pocket too: Sauve says a sleeping man's pocket is a lock with no pin at all, if you come at it low.

objectives.text: Pick the collector's strongbox: {key:interact}, then set the pin as the needle crosses
Take the tithe-book out of the strongbox
Crouched {key:sneak}, lift something from the sleeping collector's pocket {key:interact}

say: He never woke. That's the whole lesson. The key's only a key.
They look where it's loud. Be where it isn't.

stages.journal:
At first grey the collector's bravo gets up and walks his round of the landing, and his round ends at the strongbox. When he finds it open and the book gone he will go looking for it in every house on Moreva, and last tithe-day he broke Hobb's hand for a short basket. Sauve would rather he never reached the box. That is a dagger's work, and Sauve wants to see you do it once first, on a sack of eels hung from a crossbar at the landing's south-west edge.

A dagger from behind, into something that never saw you, does six times what it does to something watching. Crouch, come round to the sack's back, and put the blade in once.

objectives.text: Crouched, come at the sack from behind and strike once {key:attack_light}

say: Once. From behind. Then gone. Twice is a fight, and you don't fight.

stages.journal:
First grey, and the fog has come up off the channels like a lid. The bravo is out and walking his round of the landing with his hand on his hilt: along the south boards past the strongbox, up the east side, across between the houses, down the west side past the sack, and round again. Sooner or later he looks in the box.

Follow him crouched. When he turns, keep a house or a stack between you; when his back is to you, close and strike once. One blow from behind, before he knows you are there, ends it or nearly. If he turns on you, break his line of sight and come again. Face to face he will cut you to pieces.

objectives.round_notes: along the south boards past the strongbox, up the east side, across the landing's middle between the houses, and down the west side past the sack, clear of the gardens' fences the whole way (test_start_rogue walks it)
objectives.text: Put down the collector's bravo before he reaches the box
Crouched, from behind, before he knows you are there {key:attack_light}

stages.journal: The bravo is in the reeds. The collector woke to an open box, no book and no bravo, and he is sitting on the boards with a very good reason to say nothing to anybody. Take the tithe-book to Sauve on the landing.

give_mount.notes: tethered at the landing's end, with the Tallymen's brand on her flank

name: The Unsaid Page
description: The collector's tithe-book held, folded into its back, a Tallymen's ledger page: a village's debt, with UNSAY written across it. Somebody has paid to have a village's name struck. The collector's courier ran south at dawn with the other copy, grey in the face, as if he meant to deliver it to the Hush itself.
notes: The rogue's tie-in (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.4, 3.4a): the courier is a lead (Leads, a humanoid dressed as core:npc/tithe_courier) that keeps a field ahead by road, out of the Delta by Nauve's Landing and the Eelweir, round the Mere by Sedgehithe and Stride's Foot, and south by Merrowby (whose green the courier waits on while you turn east to the Hearthstone at Ansel's Hedge Shrine, near halfway: Merrowby has none) to the Stair Head, where he walks past the Warden's fire and down the stair, and the Naming begins at down_the_stair. The road threat is the Dodger's Stone's cutpurses, the Tallymen's own trade, up by day.

stages.journal: At first light the collector's courier was at the landing's end with his satchel buckled, looking south, grey in the face in a way that was not the fog. The page folded into the back of the tithe-book was a copy; he carries the other. Sauve's man in Gullhithe wants yours; Sauve wants to know where the other is going. Ask him.

The courier walks out of the Delta by road, by Nauve's Landing and the Eelweir, and he does not look back and he does not stop, and he keeps a field ahead of you however you come on. The bravo's horse knows the Tallymen's roads. Follow him round the Mere to Sedgehithe, and on.

objectives.text: Follow the courier out of the Delta to Sedgehithe

stages.journal: At the Dodger's Stone, on the road west of Stride's Foot, the Tallymen's cutpurses work the carts by day. The courier walked through them and they did not see him. They see you.

objectives.text: Get past the cutpurses at the Dodger's Stone

stages.journal: Merrowby, in the Vale, where the town's bell has been humming in its hole for a week and nobody will say why. The courier stopped on the green and waited for you, which a courier does not do. Merrowby keeps no Hearthstone, but a short way east along the Tamwick road is Ansel's Hedge Shrine with one in its lee: put your hand on it and say your name, so that if the road kills you it knows where to give you back. He will still be on the green.

objectives.text: Put your hand on the Hearthstone at Ansel's Hedge Shrine, east of Merrowby

stages.journal: By Wynstead and Ashwell to Pilgrim's Ash, and past the Choir's twelve headless colossi to a camp on a cliff's edge where a woman in a grey-green cloak keeps a fire at the top of a stair. The courier has stopped at the camp's edge with his satchel on his shoulder, and he is looking at the stair.

objectives.text: Speak to the Warden at the Stair Head

say: You. Tallyman. Stop. — He's not stopping. Nobody comes back up!
